title: Eager dequant merge with KV hotpath prefetch adapter and lane-aware clamps
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: latency spikes and memory pressure observed when dequantization is performed late in the ATTENTION hotpath for mixed INT8/FP8 models. This PR implements an eager dequant merge that fuses dequant ops into the kernel entry where possible, introduces a small prefetch adapter on the KV cache hotpath to warm per-lane state, and adds lane-aware clamp heuristics to stabilize scale drift for FP8 emulation. The change reduces p99 and median latency, smooths variance under bursty traffic, and avoids extra transient allocations. Changes include a new eager merge pass in the kernel router, a lightweight prefetch adapter that attaches to KVCache::read, and safe fallbacks for models that require canonical per-token dequant. Checklist: - [x] Implement eager dequant merge and kernel hook - [x] Add KV hotpath prefetch adapter with bounded async prefetch window - [x] Add per-lane clamp heuristics + config flag runtime.quant.lane_clamp - [x] Extend continuous-batcher tests to cover fused paths - [x] Benchmarks and perf tests added - [x] Security review for prefetch adapter memory access - [x] Docs updated (runtime tuning guide) Compatibility notes: the eager merge only activates for verified model signatures (quantizable weights + contiguous weight layout). For models that violate assumptions we fall back to the previous dequant-on-demand path. Linear/Jira: ENG-2184 tracks prioritization and rollout, SUP-7412 captures support cases reported during canary. Rollout plan: staged canary on Dedicated pools -> gradual ramp to hosted API with feature flag off by default for older model versions.

performance_summary: Canary benchmarks (dedicated c5-gpu pools) show median token latency -12% and p99 -18% on a suite of INT8->FP8 mixed models; throughput improved +9% under steady load with continuous-batcher enabled. Mem high-water reduced ~6% due to avoided transient allocation in the dequant path.
regressions_tested: Regression suite exercised: attention long-seq (L512), KV churn simulation, continuous-batcher with variable batch sizes, fallback to on-demand dequant path verified.
release_notes: Eager dequant fusion with KV-prefetch adapter: reduces p99 for quantized models, improves throughput and reduces transient memory. Enabled behind feature flag runtime.quant.eager_merge; default enabled for new model signatures.
notes_for_ops: Ops: when enabling feature flag at scale monitor runtime.quant.lane_clamp.* metrics and kv_prefetch_async_backoff counts. Canary observed a small uptick in KV read latency during first-minute warmups; prefetch window can be tuned via runtime.kv.prefetch_window_ms.
manual_rollback_instructions: To roll back: unset runtime.quant.eager_merge and restart runtime processes; if persistent hot objects are observed run maintenance script tools/kv/evict_prefetch_cache.sh on affected nodes.
tests_added: Added bench_fused_quant.py microbench and unit tests for lane clamps and zero-copy aliasing.
notes: This PR was coordinated with the SDK team to add a model-signature field in examples/quantized/model-signature.json; SDKs will use signature to opt-in for eager merge. Follow-up work: extend the eager merge pass to cover per-head requantization when weight layouts are split.
